Resolved from EA8074-specific downstream source (commit 06a01bad75939c58be53418f5d71d9d2e25634cf), not from the mainline helper and not from the AMS639RQ08 driver. dsi_panel.c L881-884 byte-swaps bl_lvl when qcom,mdss-dsi-bl-inverted-dbv is present, then calls mipi_dsi_dcs_set_display_brightness(); that helper (drm_mipi_dsi.c L1055-1067) packs { brightness & 0xff, brightness >> 8 } (little-endian). The EA8074 dtsi L47 DOES set qcom,mdss-dsi-bl-inverted-dbv, so the swap and the little-endian packing cancel into MSB-first. Net wire payload after DCS 0x51 = [MSB, LSB] = big-endian / most-significant-byte-first.
resolved.derivation: Let V = 0xHHLL. Swap: ((V & 0xff) << 8) | (V >> 8) = 0xLLHH. Pack little-endian: payload = [0xLLHH & 0xff, 0xLLHH >> 8] = [0xHH, 0xLL] = MSB then LSB.
resolved.mainline_equivalent: This is the same wire order that mipi_dsi_dcs_set_display_brightness_large() produces; a mainline EA8074 driver must therefore emit 0x51 with the most significant byte first and must NOT additionally byte-swap.

resolved.item: Display rail enable/disable ORDER and inter-rail delays
resolved.detail: Resolved from downstream dsi_pwr.c L136-183 (commit 06a01bad75939c58be53418f5d71d9d2e25634cf). Enable iterates the supply table forward (i = 0 .. count-1): set_load(enable_load) -> set_voltage(min,max) -> regulator_enable -> msleep(post_on_sleep). Disable iterates in reverse (i = count-1 .. 0): msleep(pre_off_sleep) -> set_load(disable_load) -> regulator_disable. The EA8074 table is entry@0 vddio (1.8 V, no sleeps) then entry@1 vci (3.0 V, post-on-sleep 10 ms, pre-off-sleep 10 ms). ENABLE order: vddio then vci, followed by a 10 ms sleep. DISABLE order: 10 ms sleep, then vci, then vddio.

resolved.item: Reset GPIO physical waveform and polarity convention
resolved.detail: Downstream dsi_panel.c L2505-2507 obtains the line via of_get_named_gpio("qcom,platform-reset-gpio") and L489-506 drives it with the raw sequence levels through legacy gpio_set_value(). The vendor DT flag is 0 (GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH), so the sequence levels map 1:1 onto physical levels: <0 2>, <1 11> = physical LOW 2 ms then HIGH 11 ms. A mainline driver using reset-gpios = <&tlmm 75 GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW> reaches the same physical waveform by writing logical 1 (assert, physical LOW) then logical 0 (release, physical HIGH). The invariant is the physical waveform; the flag only changes the logical encoding.

Both the downstream (drivers/regulator/fixed.c L85) and mainline (L194) fixed-regulator drivers read startup-delay-us. The vendor DT writes start-delay-us = <4000> on disp_vci_vreg (sirius-sdm710.dtsi L54). A repo-wide code search for "start-delay-us" returns total_count 3 and all three hits are DTS files (grus-sdm710.dtsi, sirius-sdm710.dtsi, pyxis-cosmos-sdm710-common.dtsi) - no C source reads it. Therefore the vendor 4000 us delay is inert and never applied, even in the vendor kernel. A mainline DT must use startup-delay-us = <4000> for the delay to take effect.

unresolved.item: Where the mainline 2 ms / 11 ms reset timing is encoded
unresolved.detail: This was recorded when no driver existed for the compatible: the local DTS carried no reset delay properties, so the 2/11 ms values existed only in the vendor FDT. They are now encoded in the driver this work adds -- panel-samsung-ea8074.c defines EA8074_RESET_ASSERT_MS 2 and EA8074_RESET_RELEASE_MS 11 and applies them in ea8074_reset() (assert logical 1, msleep 2, release logical 0, msleep 11). The board DTS deliberately carries no delay properties: the waveform belongs to the driver, so there is nothing to encode in the panel node.

unresolved.detail: The vendor declares 13 on-array records as data type 0x39 with a 2-byte payload (dtsi L117-L131) and the pinned mainline API emits a length-2 DCS write as 0x15 (drm_mipi_dsi.c L920-944). blockers.item: 13 vendor 0x39 long writes are emitted as 0x15 short writes
blockers.required_action: Either preserve the vendor packet type with a reviewed minimal typed DCS write helper in the DRM core (explicit design, API, guards and EXPORT, keeping the existing transfer path and padding rules, and passing its own safety review), or show with a vendor-comparable trace that the panel accepts the 0x15 form. Until then the difference must not be reported as an equivalence. See packet_type_deviation; the strict form of scripts/gen_ea8074_cmd_table.py --check-c fails on exactly this difference.
blockers.hardware_round_result: On the approved mainline round the panel powers up, the mode's pixel clock is programmed exactly (disp_cc_mdss_pclk0_clk = 165353992 Hz against the mode's own 1192*2312*60/1000 = 165354 kHz) and frames are scanned out, so the on-array records -- including the tear-on record '35 00' at index 16 -- reached the panel through the 0x15 path. This is operational evidence, not the vendor-comparable trace the blocker asks for: it cannot separate 'the panel accepts 0x15 for these records' from 'these records are tolerated and simply do nothing that the vendor type would have done'. The vblank rate observed (see mainline_hardware_round.observations.vblank) is one reason that distinction matters. This blocker stays open.

transmission_state_mechanism.note: The command state of a vendor command set is a per-set property, and the only thing that changes the wire flags is this one branch in dsi_panel_tx_cmd_set(). The DCS brightness helper takes the other path.
transmission_state_mechanism.L2232-L2235 dsi_panel_parse_cmd_sets_sub: if (!state || !strcmp(state, "dsi_lp_mode")) { cmd->state = DSI_CMD_SET_STATE_LP; } else if (!strcmp(state, "dsi_hs_mode")) { cmd->state = DSI_CMD_SET_STATE_HS; } - i.e. the on/off arrays, which carry dsi_lp_mode, become LP and an absent property defaults to LP as well
transmission_state_mechanism.L733-L781 dsi_panel_tx_cmd_set(): state = mode->priv_info->cmd_sets[type].state; for (i = 0; i < count; i++) { if (state == DSI_CMD_SET_STATE_LP) cmds->msg.flags |= MIPI_DSI_MSG_USE_LPM; ... len = ops->transfer(panel->host, &cmds->msg); } (L763-764 and L771) - so the vendor sends the on/off arrays as LP packets, exactly like the mainline MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM default
transmission_state_mechanism.L867-L890 dsi_panel_update_backlight(): the brightness path never goes through dsi_panel_tx_cmd_set(): it calls mipi_dsi_dcs_set_display_brightness(dsi, bl_lvl) directly (after the bl_inverted_dbv swap at L881), so it inherits no cmd_set state at all
transmission_state_mechanism.MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM is never assigned: A grep over the four pinned files returns exactly one occurrence of MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM, the read in drm_mipi_dsi.c L361; neither dsi_panel.c nor dsi_display.c assigns it anywhere. The vendor's own helper writes therefore do not get MIPI_DSI_MSG_USE_LPM from the mode_flags path, and the vendor DSI host sends them as HS bursts.
transmission_state_mechanism.conclusion: Vendor semantics of the three packets this driver sends: the on array and the off array (display off, sleep in) are LP; the 0x51 brightness write is HS because it is issued on a code path that carries no LP request. Mainline reaches the same split with MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM set by default and cleared around the brightness transfer only, which is what the driver does.

downstream_source_evidence.byte_order_conclusion: Derived only from EA8074-specific downstream source: dsi_panel.c L881-884 applies the bl_inverted_dbv byte swap, then drm_mipi_dsi.c L1058 packs little-endian; the EA8074 dtsi L47 enables that swap, so the two cancel and the wire payload after DCS 0x51 is [MSB, LSB].

transmission_state_evidence.question: Which of the three packets this driver sends must be LP and which must be HS, and on what evidence?
transmission_state_evidence.answer: On/off arrays in LP, brightness write in HS.
downstream_chain: dtsi L137/L138: qcom,mdss-dsi-on-command-state and -off-command-state are both "dsi_lp_mode"; L140 dimming-on is "dsi_hs_mode"; L167-169 the doze states are LP.
dsi_panel.c L2232-2235: that property becomes DSI_CMD_SET_STATE_LP / DSI_CMD_SET_STATE_HS, default LP.
dsi_panel.c L763-764 + L771: dsi_panel_tx_cmd_set() adds MIPI_DSI_MSG_USE_LPM for LP sets and only then calls ops->transfer(), so the vendor's on/off arrays are LP packets.
dsi_panel.c L867-884 (called from L1129-1183): the brightness write does not go through a command set at all, so it carries no LP request.

drm_mipi_dsi.c L361-362 (downstream): the only place that turns MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM into MIPI_DSI_MSG_USE_LPM is a read, and neither dsi_panel.c nor dsi_display.c ever assigns MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM, so the vendor's helper writes are HS.

downstream_terms.dsi_lp_mode: per-command-set property; LP packet on the wire
downstream_terms.dsi_hs_mode: per-command-set property; HS packet on the wire
downstream_terms.lp11_init: qcom,mdss-dsi-lp11-init (dtsi L36) parsed at dsi_panel.c L2374-2375; it moves the power-on from dsi_panel_pre_prepare() (which skips it, L4150-4152) to dsi_panel_prepare() (L4326-4333). It is not a per-packet state.

mainline_equivalent.note: Line numbers are 1-based in the pinned upstream tree; these files were read from it and are not part of the fixture's byte evidence.
mainline_equivalent.include/drm/drm_mipi_dsi.h L22: #define MIPI_DSI_MSG_USE_LPM BIT(1) - per-message: send this one message in low power mode
mainline_equivalent.include/drm/drm_mipi_dsi.h L138: #define MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM BIT(11) - per-device: transmit data in low power (by default)
mainline_equivalent.drivers/gpu/drm/drm_mipi_dsi.c L448-L457: mipi_dsi_device_transfer() is static and does: if (dsi->mode_flags & MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM) msg->flags |= MIPI_DSI_MSG_USE_LPM; - so MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM is the default state and clearing it makes a helper write HS. A panel driver cannot call this function (static) and must not reach host->ops->transfer itself.
mainline_equivalent.drivers/gpu/drm/drm_mipi_dsi.c L920-944: mipi_dsi_dcs_write_buffer() chooses the data type from the transmit length: 1 -> MIPI_DSI_DCS_SHORT_WRITE (0x05), 2 -> MIPI_DSI_DCS_SHORT_WRITE_PARAM (0x15), >= 3 -> MIPI_DSI_DCS_LONG_WRITE (0x39).
mainline_equivalent.drivers/gpu/drm/drm_mipi_dsi.c L1043-L10: mipi_dsi_dcs_write() concatenates { cmd, payload } and calls mipi_dsi_dcs_write_buffer(), so the 0x51 brightness write is length 3 and therefore a 0x39 long write.
mainline_equivalent.drivers/gpu/drm/drm_mipi_dsi.c L1449-L14: mipi_dsi_dcs_set_display_brightness() packs { brightness & 0xff, brightness >> 8 } and calls mipi_dsi_dcs_write(); the driver uses the _multi variant of the same helper.
mainline_equivalent.drivers/gpu/drm/msm/dsi/dsi_host.c L2178: if (!(msg->flags & MIPI_DSI_MSG_USE_LPM)) dsi_set_tx_power_mode(0|1, msm_host); - the MSM DSI host selects HS unless the message carries the LP flag, which is the concrete consequence of clearing MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM.
mainline_equivalent.drivers/gpu/drm/panel/panel-samsung-ams6: precedent for the API usage name only ("dsi->mode_flags &= ~MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM;" before a helper write). It is a different panel and is explicitly NOT evidence for the EA8074 brightness state or byte order.

driver_implementation.on_off_arrays: sent in LP: dsi->mode_flags keeps MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM, exactly the mainline default that mirrors the vendor's dsi_lp_mode sets
driver_implementation.brightness_write: sent in HS: ea8074_bl_update_status() clears MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM, performs the transfer, and restores the previous mode_flags
driver_implementation.serialisation: ea8074_bl_update_status() takes ctx->xfer_lock around the mode_flags window, and the LP sequences (on/off, and the shutdown path) take the same lock, so a mode_flags window can never overlap another packet sequence. The lock ordering is a plain mutex; no path takes it from atomic context.
driver_implementation.prepare_prev_first: kept for the lp11_init ordering requirement above, with the comment corrected: it is an API requirement of the pinned mainline core (enable the host before preparing the panel), not something claimed from a fixture property that does not exist.

residual_uncertainty: The HS/LP conclusion for the brightness write is derived from the pinned source, not from a hardware run: no packet was captured and no panel was driven. A protocol analyser trace remains the only way to confirm the state on the wire.

If a future mainline core path were to set MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM outside this driver (none does at the pinned commit), the brightness window would still be correct because it saves and restores mode_flags rather than assuming the previous value.
The vendor's on/off arrays being LP is the one part that is directly pinned by a device-tree property (dsi_lp_mode) and by the code that consumes it, so it is the stronger of the two conclusions.

packet_type_deviation.what: The pinned vendor command arrays declare 13 on-array records as data type 0x39 (long write) with a 2-byte payload. A mainline DCS write whose total length is 2 is defined to be a 0x15 short write with parameter (drm_mipi_dsi.c L920-944), and the pinned tree offers no non-static API to request 0x39 explicitly. The data type of these 13 packets therefore differs on the wire.
packet_type_deviation.why_it_cannot_be_papered_over: The bytes and the waits are identical, but the packet format is not, and the receiving panel is the only thing that can decide whether that matters. Declaring the arrays equivalent because their payloads match would be exactly the kind of unverified claim this fixture exists to prevent.
packet_type_deviation.detected_by: scripts/gen_ea8074_cmd_table.py --check-c <driver> (strict; fails on any data-type change, including this one) and --report-diff (prints the record-by-record table and passes only while the deviation is exactly this documented set)

on.emitted_types: 0x15 for those 13 records; all other records keep the vendor type (0x05 stays 0x05, 0x39 with a payload of 3 or more bytes stays 0x39)

packet_type_deviation.preserved_exactly: The 0x05 command records lose only their 0x00 pad byte (1 byte on the wire, as the vendor intends), the 0x51 record keeps its 3-byte payload and therefore its 0x39 type, the record order is unchanged, and the totals stay 21 + 2 records with the same per-record waits (120 ms for on, 37 ms + 121 ms for off) and the same array sha256.
options_considered: Resend the 13 records as a 3-byte 0x39 packet by appending a padding byte: rejected, because it would change the payload and invent a byte the vendor never sends.

Call host->ops->transfer() directly from the panel driver to pass an explicit 0x39 type: rejected, because it bypasses the DRM core's transfer wrapper with its MIPI_DSI_MODE_LPM handling, and the panel would have to reproduce the core's checks, runtime-PM and length/padding handling itself.

A minimal typed DCS core helper (for example a function that takes the intended DCS data type plus the payload, keeps the existing write buffer path and padding rules, and is EXPORT_SYMBOL'd with the same locking and PM properties as mipi_dsi_dcs_write_buffer()): this is the only option that could preserve the vendor packet types, but the API, its guards and its EXPORT must be designed and reviewed first. It is not implemented here and it must not be declared hardware-ready by this thread.
packet_type_deviation.consequence: No packet-type equivalence is claimed. The deviation is carried as blocker B2 and keeps hardware_test_ready false until it is either fixed with a reviewed typed write or shown to be harmless by a vendor-comparable trace.

outstanding.detail: A submission needs a commit message per patch -- dt-bindings: for the binding, drm/panel: for the driver, naming the panel, the device it is found in, and the reset waveform and supply order the driver reproduces -- plus one Signed-off-by per author on each. Neither patch has either yet. Drafts for both are recorded below.

This is the one thing that cannot be completed on the submitter's behalf. A Signed-off-by is a Developer Certificate of Origin assertion made by the person signing, so it is written only once the submitter says to. Until then the patches stay unsigned and the drafts below stay drafts.

The binding's maintainers entry is now the project's GitHub identity, Cocoeasy <Cocoeasy@users.noreply.github.com>. A GitHub noreply address is deliverable through GitHub, but a mainline binding usually wants the author's real name and an address they control, and reviewers do ask. The submitter should confirm this is what they want published or give a replacement before the series goes out.

0001_dt_bindings.subject: dt-bindings: display: panel: add Samsung EA8074
body: Document the Samsung EA8074, a 5.88 inch 1080x2244 MIPI-DSI command mode AMOLED panel with a 10-bit DCS brightness control, as found in the Xiaomi Mi 8 SE (xiaomi-sirius, SDM710).
The panel takes a 1.8 V I/O rail and a 3.0 V source rail and a single active-low reset line; the reset waveform itself is the driver's business and is not described here.
Signed-off-by: (to be added by the submitter)

0002_drm_panel.subject: drm/panel: samsung: add EA8074
body: Add a driver for the Samsung EA8074 command mode AMOLED panel (1080x2244) found in the Xiaomi Mi 8 SE.

The mode, lane count, reset waveform, supply order and delays, on/off command arrays and brightness encoding all come from the panel's vendor device tree and driver at SDM710-Development/android_kernel_xiaomi_sdm710@06a01bad; the API usage follows panel-samsung-ams639rq08.c, a command mode AMOLED panel on the same DSI host.

One deviation is deliberate and is called out in the driver, not hidden: 13 vendor records use DCS long write (0x39) with a two-byte payload, and the exported helper derives the data type from the buffer length, so those go out as 0x15 short-write-with-parameter with the same command and parameter. Whether the panel accepts 0x15 there is not verified. Closing it needs either hardware confirmation or a typed-DCS helper in the DRM core, which is a separate change and is not part of this patch.
Signed-off-by: (to be added by the submitter)
